title: Annual error updates raised cherry interval coverage but gave no clear common score gain in four Japan samples in 1993-2025
abstract: We tested annual error updates for 90 percent intervals of cherry first-to-full bloom gaps. We reused a verified panel of JMA phenology and NOAA temperature. Four tests used separate northern and southern stations and later periods in 1993-2025. Fixed weather models kept their original coefficients. A median shift and width update from the previous ten complete years raised coverage from 74-85 percent to 87-90 percent. All four primary score-gain limits included zero. The largest estimated gain, in the later South, fell from 3.63 to 0.11 days when the fixed model omitted a time trend. Thus better coverage did not establish a clear common score gain, and trend extrapolation explains part of the largest estimated benefit. Selected stations, unknown visits and tree changes, post-event monthly weather and uncertainty conditional on calibration histories limit inference. This is a method test on reused records, not an independent data replication or a causal climate result.

display.caption: Annual error updates raised coverage. The four primary center-update score intervals span zero. Orange width-only comparisons are diagnostic. Limits condition on fitted models and realized calibration histories.
